page: Microsoft Azure E96-24s_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine utilizing a constrained core configuration. Built on the x86_64 architecture and running under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance features an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz. The configuration allocates 12 physical cores and 24 dedicated vCPUs with 2 threads per core, backed by 105 MB of L3 cache. It pairs these 24 vCPUs with 672.0 GB of system memory, resulting in an exceptionally high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 28.0 GB per vCPU. No local temporary storage is attached, requiring remote block storage for data persistence, and no discrete GPUs are present.

Benchmark results reflect the instance's high-capacity memory architecture. The virtual machine demonstrates strong memory throughput, achieving 106.74 GB/sec in large-block uncached memory write tests and a PassMark memory score of 2894.78, both placing in the top 25 percent of tested systems. Multi-core compute performance sits in the middle 50 percent, delivering a PassMark CPU score of 30451.25, a multi-core stress-ng rating of 23302.98, and a Geekbench multi-core score of 12123.0. In network and in-memory workload tests, it achieved 23.93 million operations per second for Redis SET requests and 28.2 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

By constraining the execution environment to 24 vCPUs while retaining the full 672.0 GB memory footprint of an enterprise-tier chassis, the E96-24s_v5 optimizes licensing efficiency for software billed on a per-core basis. The primary tradeoff is the absence of bundled local NVMe storage and average per-core compute output. This configuration is engineered primarily for memory-bound applications, including large-scale relational databases, in-memory caches, analytics engines, and enterprise resource planning software requiring extensive memory capacity without requiring excessive core counts.
description: Microsoft Azure E96-24s_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Designed as a constrained-core configuration, it offers 24 dedicated vCPUs across 12 physical cores paired with 672.0 GB of RAM, yielding an expansive 28.0 GB of memory per vCPU. The instance includes no bundled local storage or GPUs, relying on remote managed disks. Benchmark assessments indicate top-tier memory performance, recording 106.74 GB/sec in uncached large-block memory writes and a PassMark memory score in the upper quartile, alongside mid-range multi-core CPU metrics. This structure offers a cost-effective design for workloads governed by per-core software licensing, making it particularly appropriate for large in-memory databases, enterprise relational database management systems, and memory-intensive analytics workloads.
